model.name: Goal / Objective
model.purpose: Represent a desired outcome as a governable record: what end state is wanted, for whom and by when, how attainment is measured, who is accountable, on what authority it stands, and how it is refined, changed and superseded — without owning the actions that pursue it, the metrics that measure it, or the systems that evaluate it.
model.scope_statement: In scope is the declarative content of a goal or objective record and the parameters that make it operable by an agent: statement, role (overall objective vs derived target), classification, identity and codes, measure binding by reference, baseline and target value with unit and scope, time horizon and interim milestones, refinement and contribution structure, accountability and mandate, declared status and change control, provenance, definition quality and external alignments. Out of scope is anything that happens when the goal is pursued or measured: planning and execution of actions, collection or computation of indicator values, evaluation verdicts, enforcement, incentives and audit-trail keeping. Sources consistently separate objective (overall end), target (detailed derived performance requirement) and indicator (measurement expression), and assign 'how results will be evaluated' to action planning rather than to the objective itself.
in_scope: Goal statement semantics: subject of change, direction, end-state condition and achievement criteria
Role distinction between overall objective, derived target and referenced indicator
Identity, governed codes and canonical wording (including language variants) of the goal record
Target parameters: baseline value, base year/period, target value, unit, absolute vs relative, tolerance and scope boundary
Time horizon, target year or period, interim targets and milestones as declared parameters
Refinement (AND/OR), contribution and alignment to higher-level ends
Declared conflicts, trade-offs and priority among goals (declaration, not runtime arbitration)
Accountability assignment: owner, lead/responsible official, contributors, approver
Authority and mandate basis: statutory, contractual, board-approved or voluntary; binding vs aspirational
Goal-record lifecycle status, review cadence triggers, restatement and supersession
Provenance of the goal record, including event time versus ingestion time
Definition quality and structural validation of the goal record
Alignment mappings to external goal/target frameworks and declared conflicts with them
Disclosure status and retention/disposition references for superseded goal records
out_of_scope: Indicator/metric definitions, computation methods and data collection procedures (measure model owns these; the goal only carries a reference and target parameters)
Observation values, time series and progress data points used to judge attainment
Evaluation verdicts, scoring engines, performance appraisal and any runtime attainment computation
Planning, scheduling, resourcing and execution of the actions or programmes that pursue the goal (parent action model)
Policy, rule and requirement enforcement, permission evaluation and compliance determination
Risk identification, assessment and treatment records
Decision and approval records themselves (referenced, not reproduced)
Audit trails, records-management disposition execution and evidential retention operations
Party/organisation and role master data
Budget, funding and incentive/compensation mechanics
Published reports or disclosures that contain goals (rendering artefacts of other models)

boundary_notes.distinction: EMAS defines an environmental performance indicator as 'a specific expression that allows measurement of an organisation's environmental performance', separate from objective and target; ESRS separates minimum disclosures for metrics (MDR-M) from targets (MDR-T). This model carries an indicator reference, unit and target parameters only.
Actual values, coverage and periodicity of measurement belong to the observation model; only baseline value, base year and target value are held here as declared parameters of the commitment.

EMAS clause 6.2.2 assigns 'what will be done, what resources will be required, who will be responsible, when it will be completed, how the results will be evaluated' to planning of actions. This model records the end state and its accountability, not the plan or its execution.

EMAS derives objectives from the environmental policy; policy is the standing normative frame, the objective is the result sought. Obligation expression, enforcement and permission evaluation stay in the policy model.
Objectives are the reference point against which risk is expressed; risk registers, likelihood/impact assessment and treatment plans are not modelled here, only referenced.
The act of approving, adopting or withdrawing a goal is a decision record owned elsewhere; this model stores the approval reference, the resulting authority basis and the effective period.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Agent task/request model (e.g. ROS 2 action goals)
boundary_notes.distinction: An execution goal is a request with a server-side state machine (ACCEPTED, EXECUTING, CANCELING, SUCCEEDED, ABORTED, CANCELED) owned by the executing system. That state machine is not imported; this model keeps only the standing goal record's declared status.

ESRS target disclosures are rendered inside a sustainability statement; the statement, its structure and its assurance are a reporting artefact, while the target definition itself is the governed record here.
This model declares retention class, tombstone and supersession references; physical disposition and its evidence are executed under the adopting Dimension's records policy.

findings.name: Desired-outcome statement
findings.description: The end state the goal requires — subject, direction of change and condition of satisfaction — expressed independently of the means used to reach it.

data_elements.name: Goal statement text
data_elements.description: Canonical normative wording of the desired outcome.

data_elements.name: Direction of change code
data_elements.description: Coded direction of the intended change in the subject's state.

data_elements.name: Achievement criterion
data_elements.description: Expression of the condition under which the goal counts as achieved.

data_elements.name: Quantification practicable flag
data_elements.description: Whether quantification of the objective is practicable, per EMAS 'quantified where practicable'.

findings.name: Objective, target and indicator roles
findings.description: Rules that place a record as an overall objective, a derived detailed target, or neither — the indicator being a measurement expression owned by another model.

data_elements.name: Record role code
data_elements.description: Whether the record is an overall objective, a derived target, or an aspiration without a target.

data_elements.name: Parent objective reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the objective that this target details.

data_elements.name: Naming regime
data_elements.description: The external regime whose vocabulary is used (EMAS, GPRAMA, ESRS, SDG) so that 'target' is read correctly.

findings.name: Goal classification scheme
findings.description: Controlled vocabularies typing the goal by level, result type, obligation status and measurability so agents can select comparable goals.

data_elements.name: Goal level code
data_elements.description: Strategic, tactical or operational placement of the goal.

data_elements.name: Result type code
data_elements.description: Whether the goal is expressed as an outcome, output or process result.

data_elements.name: Obligation status code
data_elements.description: Mandated or voluntary status of the goal.

data_elements.name: Classification scheme version
data_elements.description: Version identifier of the code list used for each assigned code.

findings.name: Goal identity and governed codes
findings.description: The identifier set that makes a goal citable: authoritative register identifier, governed external codes and a locally minted fallback.

data_elements.name: Master system identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier issued by the authoritative register that owns the goal.

data_elements.name: Governed external code
data_elements.description: Code assigned by an external governed scheme, such as an SDG target code.

data_elements.name: Locally minted identifier
data_elements.description: UUIDv7 or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension where no authoritative identifier exists.

findings.name: Official wording and language variants
findings.description: Control of the authoritative wording, translations and short labels, and of changes to wording that do not change the goal's substance.

data_elements.name: Statement language tag
data_elements.description: BCP 47 language tag of each wording variant, with the authoritative variant marked.

data_elements.name: Short label
data_elements.description: Abbreviated display label for the goal.

data_elements.name: Wording change class
data_elements.description: Classification of a wording change as editorial or substantive.

findings.name: Measure binding by reference
findings.description: The reference from the goal to one or more indicator or metric definitions, with the parameters this goal contributes and nothing of the measure's own definition.

data_elements.name: Measure definition reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the indicator or metric definition used to judge progress, owned by the measure model.

data_elements.name: Unit of measure
data_elements.description: Unit in which the target and baseline values are expressed.

data_elements.name: Qualitative progress basis
data_elements.description: Declared qualitative criteria used where no measurable target is set.

findings.name: Target value, baseline and base period
findings.description: The quantified commitment: baseline value and base year, target value with unit, absolute or relative form, tolerance and threshold direction.

data_elements.name: Baseline value
data_elements.description: Value from which progress is measured.

data_elements.name: Base year or base period
data_elements.description: Calendar year or period to which the baseline value refers, expressed as a period code, not as an identifier.

data_elements.name: Target value
data_elements.description: Value or level to be achieved.

data_elements.name: Absolute or relative flag
data_elements.description: Whether the target is expressed in absolute terms or relative to the baseline or another denominator.

data_elements.name: Achievement comparison operator
data_elements.description: Operator defining satisfaction against the target value (at least, at most, equal, within band).

findings.name: Methodology, scenario and assumptions
findings.description: The significant assumptions, scenarios, data sources and evidence basis on which the target value was set, disclosed so the target can be challenged.

data_elements.description: Narrative of how the target value was derived.

data_elements.name: Significant assumptions

data_elements.name: Scientific basis flag

data_elements.name: Period convention

data_elements.name: Milestone type
data_elements.description: Whether the milestone is a measured interim value or a scheduled deliverable event.

findings.name: Scope, exclusions and external conditions

data_elements.name: Geographic scope

data_elements.name: External condition assumed

data_elements.name: Contribution link

functions.name: Bind measure and target parameters

functions.name: Refine goal
functions.description: Record AND/OR refinement into sub-goals and typed contribution links to other goals or qualities.

functions.name: Assign accountability

functions.name: Transition goal state
functions.description: Move the goal record between declared statuses with reason, actor and effective time.

functions.name: Restate target
functions.description: Apply a controlled change to a target value, baseline, scope or methodology and preserve comparability.

functions.name: Record external alignment

composition.target: WM-ACT-008 — Action / Activity (registered parent model)
composition.purpose: The goal is the intended end state of action; this model is registered beneath the action model, which retains planning, resourcing, scheduling and execution of the means (EMAS clause 6.2.2 assigns what, resources, who, when and how results are evaluated to action planning).

composition.target: Indicator / measure definition model (sibling; identifier to be assigned by the registry)
composition.purpose: Carry an indicator reference, unit and the goal-specific target parameters only; the indicator's definition, computation method, data sources and periodicity remain owned by the measure model.

composition.target: Measurement / observation (time series) model (sibling; identifier to be assigned)
composition.purpose: Reference observed values and assessment outputs used to support a status claim; no observation values, aggregation or progress computation are stored or performed here.

composition.target: Party / organisation / role model (sibling; identifier to be assigned)
composition.purpose: Resolve accountable party, contributors, record steward and authorising roles; party master data and appointment lifecycle stay in that model.

composition.target: Policy / rule / requirement model (sibling; identifier to be assigned)
composition.purpose: Cite the governing policy the objective must be consistent with and the constraints bounding permissible target values; obligation expression, evaluation and enforcement remain in that model.

composition.target: Decision / approval model (sibling; identifier to be assigned)
composition.purpose: Cite the decision that approved, revised or withdrew the goal; the deliberation, voting and decision record structure are not reproduced here.

composition.target: Risk model (sibling; identifier to be assigned)
composition.purpose: Link risks registered against achievement of the goal, since risk is expressed relative to objectives; assessment, treatment and monitoring stay in the risk model.

composition.target: Records management / retention model of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Declare retention class and tombstone expectations for superseded goal records; scheduling, execution and evidence of disposition are owned there.

composition.target: Provenance mixin aligned to W3C PROV-O
composition.purpose: Reuse Entity/Activity/Agent attribution, derivation and qualified-influence patterns for goal-record provenance instead of defining a local provenance vocabulary.

composition.target: UN SDG global indicator framework (goal, target and indicator codes)
composition.purpose: Map goal records to SDG target codes as an external governed scheme, recording framework version and mapping strength; the SDG framework's custodianship and refinement process are external.

composition.target: ESRS 2 minimum disclosure requirement for targets (MDR-T)
composition.purpose: Align target attributes (baseline, base year, unit, scope, period, milestones, methodology, changes) with the reporting datapoints, without adopting the sustainability statement's preparation or assurance process.

composition.target: GPRA Modernization Act performance goal, indicator and milestone definitions (31 U.S.C. 1115)
composition.purpose: Align the target-level-of-performance and lead-official concepts for public-sector goal records; the statutory planning and reporting cycle itself is out of scope.

composition.target: iStar 2.0 goal modelling constructs (goal, quality, refinement, contribution, dependency)
composition.purpose: Adopt refinement and contribution semantics for goal structure while leaving actor-dependency analysis and requirements-engineering method to that language.

providerPolicy.scope: Queued subject-model research from WM-XCT-013 onward

waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two axes must not be conflated. On the record-plane axis the frozen registry value 'standalone-mm' stays correct: it classifies vr.wm-knw-011 as a standalone mega-model registry row rather than a sub-entry of another record, and it says nothing about the thing modelled. On the subject-model axis the defensible schema kind is 'entity': the goal record carries identity independent of its attribute values (master identifier, then governed code or IRI, then minted UUIDv7/ULID), keeps that identity through editorial change, restatement and supersession, has a declared lifecycle with terminal statuses and a resolvable tombstone, and is answerable to a single named accountable party. 'aggregate' was seriously tested and rejected: restatement notes, conformance checklists, milestone schedules and target specification sheets are all identified by goal identity plus a local discriminator, and the patch rule (single goal record version, expected preceding version, rejection on staleness) reads like an aggregate consistency boundary, but three declared artifacts (goal type code list, accountability assignment record, alignment crosswalk) are mastered by external vocabulary, HR/governance and mapping registers, so no closed transactional boundary over the artifact set can be asserted. 'relationship' is rejected because refinement, contribution and alignment are typed outgoing references held by the record rather than the subject of the model; 'classifier' is rejected because the code lists are consumed and version-pinned here, not governed here; 'event' is rejected because status transitions and approvals are recorded as coded state with effective time while the approval act itself is owned by the decision model.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root identity: the canonical goal record
decisions.rationale: Every serial and derived artifact (target specification sheet, milestone schedule, restatement note, conformance checklist, provenance statement, refinement map) is identified from goal identity plus a register-issued discriminator, so the root is unambiguous. The exceptions must be stated in the draft: goal type code list, accountability assignment and alignment crosswalk are mastered elsewhere and are therefore referenced members, not owned parts.

decisions.concept: art-goal-type-code-list as an owned artifact of fd-goal-classification
decisions.disposition: rejected as owned; retain as referenced external artifact
decisions.rationale: The owner package requirements already assign publication and versioning of the goal type code list to the owning vocabulary register, and the model refuses local re-implementation of sibling functions. Holding the code list as a produced artifact here makes the goal model a classifier of its own typing vocabulary and creates the second divergent definition the measure-binding rationale explicitly forbids.

decisions.concept: Single entity with record-role code versus separate Goal and Target model entries
decisions.disposition: accepted (single entity plus role code and naming-regime tag)
decisions.rationale: The cited regimes invert vocabulary (EMAS objective-versus-target, 31 U.S.C. 1115 performance goal as a target level, ISO using objective for both) but agree on a derived-detail relation. A role code with a naming-regime tag preserves both readings without privileging one legal vocabulary, and splitting would duplicate identity, lifecycle and provenance machinery across two entries.

decisions.concept: SRC-009 (ROS 2 Actions) cited as positive support for fd-goal-identity, fd-goal-status-and-review and fn-transition-goal-state
decisions.disposition: rejected as positive support; retained only as boundary counterexample
decisions.rationale: The model states that the ROS 2 action-goal state machine is owned by the executing server, describes a request rather than a standing commitment, and is deliberately not imported. Citing it as source support for standing-record identity and for the state-transition function contradicts the model's own boundary note; those three support links must be re-anchored to SRC-001, SRC-002 and SRC-004 or the citation reduced to the boundary note where it already sits.

decisions.concept: SRC-010 (ISO committee explanatory page) supporting the strategic/tactical/operational level vocabulary
decisions.disposition: deferred; mark as unsupported structure pending evidence
decisions.rationale: SRC-010 is the only non-primary source in the pack (tier 2, primary_source false) and the known omissions concede that ISO 9000:2015 term 3.7.1 could not be retrieved. The goal-level taxonomy in q-goal-level therefore rests on an explanatory web page, and should carry the same visible 'unsupported structure pending evidence' marking already applied to localisation rather than sitting silently as covered.

decisions.concept: Localisation and authoritative-language equivalence
decisions.disposition: accepted as a declared gap; hold must stay visible
decisions.rationale: The coverage checklist already records localisation as the single gap and states that no primary source governs translation equivalence for goal statements. That honesty is upheld, but fd-goal-wording-and-language must be published with the gap marking attached to the finding itself, not only in the checklist, so a reader of the structure cannot mistake it for evidenced content.

decisions.concept: Milestone typing overlap with the plan/schedule model
decisions.rationale: GPRAMA defines a milestone as a scheduled event signifying completion of a deliverable, which leans toward the plan model, while ESRS interim targets are commitments. Keeping milestones as declared interim commitments with the overlap recorded is the defensible interim position, but q-milestone-significance is currently the only mechanism separating the two readings and cannot settle ownership without a primary source.

decisions.concept: Audit-trail custody
decisions.rationale: Out-of-scope, policies, the status finding rationale and access.audit_requirements agree: reason, actor and event time are held locally while the immutable trail belongs to the adopting Dimension's audit model. The adversarial check that no cited source grants audit custody is sound and the residual local fields are the minimum needed to make a change attributable, not a trail.

decisions.concept: Retention declared as class and pointer, disposition executed elsewhere
decisions.rationale: The delete rules, the retention finding, the boundary note against the records-management model and the tombstone content specification are mutually consistent: no physical delete, comparability retention enforced, disposition and its evidence assigned outward, privacy erasure routed to the Dimension policy with only the restriction recorded here. No source in the pack grants disposition authority, so the outward assignment is correct.

decisions.concept: Access control fields versus the declared access scope vocabulary
decisions.rationale: Restricting evaluation and enforcement to the access model is correct and evidenced by the disclosure finding rationale. However the declared scopes (bundle, layer, finding, artifact) are research-structure granularities and do not name the record elements the exceptions actually govern: embargo audiences, individual-identifying goals shared only in aggregate, and tombstones readable when the withdrawn content was restricted. The mismatch is a coherence gap to resolve at specification time, not a blocker for a draft.

decisions.concept: Artifact identity and timestamp rules across all twelve artifacts
decisions.rationale: Every identity_strategy applies the same three-step priority, every one bars date-based identity, and the base-year and target-year prohibition is repeated in the timestamp rule. The two serial artifacts (restatement note, conformance checklist) are exactly the ones that recur per goal, their sequences are register-issued, non-reusable and gap-annotated, and the integrity rule forbids silent digest repair. This is the strongest internally verified part of the result.

decisions.concept: Frozen registry parent_ids WM-ACT-008 against nav path NAV.INF.KNW.GOL
decisions.rationale: The registry asserts an action-plane parent while the nav path and domain tags place the model under information/knowledge, and the model's own boundary note says it records the end state and its accountability rather than the plan or its execution. The link is defensible as 'pursued by' or 'served by' but not as containment; it must be re-expressed as a typed relation or re-parented before the record leaves candidate status.

decisions.concept: Empty relationship contract against nine declared sibling dependencies
decisions.disposition: accepted for a reviewable draft; blocking for specification promotion
decisions.rationale: The frozen relationship contract is an empty array and the registry lists no contains_ids or aligned_model_ids, yet the whole boundary strategy routes measurement, observation, action, policy, decision, risk, party, access and retention outward to models whose identifiers the service layer itself admits are 'to be assigned'. The structure is readable and reviewable as a draft, but its exclusions are currently unenforceable.

decisions.concept: Function-set gaps: disclosure/embargo change, conformance-check execution, priority declaration, means linkage
decisions.rationale: Ten functions cover registration through withdrawal, but the disclosure and access authority role decides publication, embargo and redaction with no function to record it after creation; the steward runs conformance checks that produce a serial artifact with no function; and fd-goal-conflict-and-priority and fd-means-and-action-linkage produce declarations no function writes. Under the waiver no functions may be added, so these are logged for the specification stage.

decisions.concept: Optional measurability with mandatory justification
decisions.rationale: The adversarial check is sound and evidenced on both sides: EMAS quantifies only where practicable and ESRS provides a fallback where no measurable target exists, while iStar 2.0 demands clear-cut achievement criteria. Making the measure optional but the non-practicability justification mandatory, with a qualitative basis and base period recorded, is the narrowest position the cited sources support.

publicationHolds: Live source and version verification hold: all ten source URLs must be re-fetched and their cited pins confirmed before publication, in particular SRC-006 (a live SDG indicator list cited at the 2026 refinement, E/CN.3/2026/12 Annex I), SRC-004 (EFRAG interactive ESRS Set 1 rendering including the 2025-11-10 quick fix), SRC-005 (consolidated Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 applicable from 1 January 2025) and SRC-010 (an undated ISO committee page cited as accessed September 2026). Any URL that no longer returns the cited version invalidates the findings that rest on it.

Single-provider hold: independent second-provider review is absent by explicit repository-owner authorization (grok waived at 2026-08-29T09:06:27Z after repeated structured-output failures). No cross-provider agreement exists for entry kind, bundles, layers, findings, questions, artifacts or functions; every published artifact must carry a visible single-provider notice and the result remains a reviewable draft, not a validated model.

Registry-plane hold: the frozen record is status 'candidate' with review_state 'boundary-review-required', and its entry_kind value 'standalone-mm' classifies the registry row rather than the subject model. The published draft must show both axes side by side (record plane 'standalone-mm', subject-model kind 'entity') so no reader treats the registry value as the model's kind.

Unregistered-boundary hold: the frozen relationship contract is empty and the composition ledger identifiers for the measure, observation, party, policy, decision, risk, access and retention models are unassigned. The model's exclusions of measurement, execution, evaluation, enforcement and disposition are therefore declared but not contractually enforceable, and the draft must say so.

Source-support hold: before publication, downgrade or re-anchor the SRC-009 (ROS 2) citations on goal identity, status/review and the state-transition function to the standing-commitment sources, and mark the SRC-010-backed goal-level taxonomy and the localisation structure as unsupported pending evidence, so evidence strength is visible at the finding level and not only in the coverage checklist.
Independent second-provider review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this Claude-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Retrieve OMG Business Motivation Model 1.3 by alternative PDF text extraction or an authoritative secondary rendering, and test its Goal-versus-Objective distinction against the record-role code adopted here.

Obtain licensed access to ArchiMate 3.2 motivation elements (Goal, Outcome, Driver, Assessment) that are currently behind an authentication redirect, and record an alignment crosswalk entry with an explicit mapping strength.

Obtain a licensed copy of ISO 9000:2015 term 3.7.1 ('objective: result to be achieved'), which returned HTTP 403 from the ISO Online Browsing Platform, and use it to replace or confirm the non-primary ISO committee page now supporting the goal-level taxonomy.

Find a primary source governing authoritative-language and translation equivalence for goal statements (for example the equal-authenticity rules for EU language versions) to close the declared localisation gap.

Find a primary source that settles milestone ownership between the goal record and the plan/schedule model, so interim commitments and scheduled deliverable events can be separated by evidence rather than by declaration.

Test target-attribute mandates outside the EU and US instruments cited here (other national performance, sustainability or reporting regimes) to check whether the regional assumptions understate required goal attributes.

Resolve the registry parent link: determine whether WM-ACT-008 is a containment parent or a typed 'pursued by' relation, given that the nav path places this model under information/knowledge and the boundary notes deny ownership of plan and execution.

model.name: Observable Result Fields
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral field group for expressing an observation or measurement result — measurand binding, value, unit and quantity kind, method reference, uncertainty, limits, time anchoring, state, provenance and disclosure class — so that any host record can carry an interpretable, comparable result without forking metrology semantics.
model.scope_statement: This mixin defines the fields that make a reported value interpretable and comparable, and the rules that govern them. It attaches to a host record (registered parent WM-MAT-008 and any other adopting host) and carries references into vocabularies, procedures, devices, samples, access policy and conformity-decision models without reproducing their lifecycles. Storage and interface (JSON, RDF, Markdown, Git, MCP, MongoDB) are projections of these semantics, never their definition.
in_scope: Measurand and observed-property binding, including specified conditions and property class (quantity, ordinal, nominal)
Value representation: scalar, coded, ordinal, boolean, range, ratio, component/tuple and reference to an external series
Unit code and code-system binding, quantity kind, dimensional commensurability, canonical expression alongside the as-reported value
Numeric precision, declared resolution and rounding rules
Reference to the procedure or method and the subject-specific parameters and influence quantities that qualify the value
Uncertainty statement: components, evaluation type, distribution, combined standard uncertainty, coverage factor and coverage probability
Detection and quantitation limits, comparator operators and censored values
Phenomenon (event) time, result time and ingestion time, validity window and aggregation period
Result status, supersession and amendment linkage; coded absence of a value
Derivation and assertion lineage, evidence references and digests
Sensitivity classification, redaction signalling and retention class recorded as references
out_of_scope: The observation act, sampling activity and their scheduling (owned by an observation/event model)
Sensor, device and platform registration, calibration execution and certificate issuance
Minting, deprecation or maintenance of unit codes, quantity kinds and conversion factor tables
Authoring, validation studies and approval lifecycle of procedures and methods
Feature-of-interest, sample and specimen definition and custody
Numerical propagation of distributions through a measurement model (performed by the producing measurement system)
Conformity assessment, acceptance decisions, guard banding and pass/fail rules
Access evaluation, enforcement, audit-trail storage and physical disposition execution
Time-series, coverage and statistical dataset storage, indexing and compression
Laboratory accreditation, quality-management and competence claims
Alerting, clinical or operational decision support acting on a result

boundary_notes.neighbor: Observation act / event model (sosa:Observation, OMS Observation)
boundary_notes.distinction: The act carries exactly one result; this mixin defines the result payload's fields and their interpretation rules. It does not own the act, its sampling features, its stimulus or its scheduling.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Sensor, device and calibration record model
boundary_notes.distinction: This mixin carries an observer/device reference and a calibration record reference plus a validity-at-observation check. Device lifecycle, calibration execution and certificate issuance stay with that model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Unit and quantity-kind vocabulary registry (UCUM, QUDT, UN/CEFACT Rec 20)
boundary_notes.distinction: This mixin pins a code system version and cites codes, quantity kinds and conversion factors by reference. Code minting, deprecation and factor maintenance are the registry's.
This mixin carries a method identifier, version and subject-specific parameter overrides. Method authoring, validation studies and approval remain in the catalogue.
Interpretation flags and a reference to an applied reference interval are carried here as context; acceptance, pass/fail and guard-band decisions and their records belong to the decision model.
Referenced only, to anchor what the value is about; sample identity, hierarchy and custody are not modelled here.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Access policy, audit and retention model of the adopting Dimension
boundary_notes.distinction: As FHIR separates Observation from its security and audit resources, this mixin records a sensitivity class, a policy reference and a retention class only; evaluation, enforcement, audit-trail storage and disposition execution are external.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Time-series / statistical dataset model (SensorThings Datastream, FHIR SampledData)
boundary_notes.distinction: When the result is a large series the mixin holds a reference plus the fields needed to interpret it; series storage, windowing and aggregation infrastructure are external.

findings.name: Measurand binding and specification
findings.description: A value is meaningless without the property it quantifies, the entity that property belongs to, and the conditions under which it was specified; VIM treats a result as quantity values attributed to a measurand plus all other relevant information.

data_elements.name: Observed property code
data_elements.description: Governed code identifying the property observed.

data_elements.name: Measurand specification
data_elements.description: Narrative or referenced specification of the measurand including conditions of measurement.

data_elements.name: Feature of interest reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the entity or sample whose property was observed; the entity itself is modelled elsewhere.

data_elements.name: Property class
data_elements.description: Whether the property is a quantity, an ordinal property or a nominal property.

findings.name: Value kind and primitive carriage
findings.description: FHIR carries thirteen value[x] alternatives and SOSA offers both a simple literal result and a structured Result object; a reusable field group must fix which shape a host property uses and how the primitive is carried.

data_elements.name: Result value
data_elements.description: The polymorphic value slot whose concrete shape is fixed by the binding profile.

data_elements.name: Value representation kind
data_elements.description: Code naming the concrete shape used (quantity, coded, boolean, range, ratio, series reference and so on).

data_elements.name: Declared precision
data_elements.description: Explicit statement of the significant digits carried by the value as reported.

findings.name: Structured, coded and referenced results
findings.description: Composite observations (components), bounded results (range, ratio), ordinal and nominal codes, and results too large to embed all need declared structure and ordering.

data_elements.name: Result components
data_elements.description: Ordered set of coded component values belonging to one observation.

data_elements.name: Permissible value set reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the governed code list and version constraining a coded or ordinal result.

data_elements.name: External series reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a series, waveform or datastream carrying the result payload.

findings.name: Mixin attachment contract
findings.description: As a mixin, the group has no standalone record; its attachment point, cardinality, mandatory subset and namespace must be declared per host record type.

data_elements.name: Host record reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the record instance carrying the field group.

data_elements.name: Binding profile identifier
data_elements.description: Versioned identifier of the profile that fixes value kinds, unit systems and mandatory fields for the host.

data_elements.name: Field namespace prefix
data_elements.description: Dimension-scoped prefix applied to group fields to prevent host collisions.

findings.name: Unit code and code system pinning
findings.description: FHIR separates a human-readable unit from a system-plus-code pair; UCUM's code space is open, so the code system and its version must be pinned rather than assumed.

data_elements.name: Unit code
data_elements.description: Machine-processable unit code drawn from the pinned code system.

data_elements.name: Unit code system
data_elements.description: URI of the code system from which the unit code is drawn.

data_elements.name: Unit code system version
data_elements.description: Version of the unit code system pinned at the time the record was created.

data_elements.name: Unit display label
data_elements.description: Human-readable unit rendering, never authoritative for processing.

findings.name: Quantity kind and dimensional consistency
findings.description: OMS requires the result scale to suit the observed property; QUDT's dimension vectors make that check computable rather than editorial.

data_elements.name: Quantity kind reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the governed quantity kind expected for the property.

data_elements.name: Dimension vector
data_elements.description: Dimensional signature used to test commensurability.

data_elements.name: Commensurability verdict
data_elements.description: Stored outcome of the unit-to-quantity-kind check.

findings.name: Precision, resolution and rounding
findings.description: FHIR states that decimal precision is significant and must be preserved; resolution of the method is distinct from uncertainty and must not be conflated with it.

data_elements.name: Numeric value
data_elements.description: The reported number, carried so that declared precision is preserved.

data_elements.name: Significant digits
data_elements.description: Count of significant digits in the reported number.

data_elements.name: Reported resolution
data_elements.description: Smallest change the producing method or instrument can distinguish, expressed as a quantity.

data_elements.name: Rounding rule
data_elements.description: Named rule governing presentation or re-encoding at reduced precision.

findings.name: As-reported value and canonical expression
findings.description: Comparison across records often needs a canonical unit, but the as-reported value must remain authoritative and the conversion must be attributable.

data_elements.name: As-reported expression
data_elements.description: The value and unit exactly as supplied by the producing system.

data_elements.name: Canonical expression
data_elements.description: Derived value and unit in the profile's canonical unit, labelled as derived.

data_elements.name: Conversion factor reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the registry entry supplying the multiplier and offset used.

data_elements.name: Conversion applied at
data_elements.description: Time the canonical expression was computed, distinct from phenomenon and result time.

findings.name: Method and procedure reference
findings.description: The mixin cites the procedure, algorithm or process chain and its version; authoring and approval of that procedure belong to the method catalogue.

data_elements.name: Procedure reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the procedure or method used.

data_elements.name: Procedure version
data_elements.description: Version or revision of the cited procedure applicable to this result.

data_elements.name: Method disclosure status
data_elements.description: Whether the method is public, restricted, proprietary or unknown.

findings.name: Conditions and qualifying parameters
findings.description: SensorThings carries structured parameters on an observation and OMS allows observation parameters; influence quantities that change interpretation must travel with the value.

data_elements.name: Result parameter set
data_elements.description: Named parameters and influence quantities qualifying the result.

data_elements.name: Correction applied indicator
data_elements.description: Whether a correction for a stated influence quantity has been applied to the value.

findings.name: Traceability and calibration reference
findings.description: VIM defines traceability as a documented unbroken chain of calibrations; the mixin carries the reference and a validity check, never the calibration process.

data_elements.name: Metrological reference
data_elements.description: The reference (standard, certified material or stated reference) to which the value is traceable.

data_elements.name: Calibration record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the calibration record held by the device or calibration model.

data_elements.name: Traceability claim status
data_elements.description: Whether traceability is claimed, partially documented, absent or not applicable.

findings.name: Observer and accountable organisation
findings.description: SOSA allows a sensor to be a device, a human or a computational process; a defensible result identifies the observer and the organisation accountable for it.

data_elements.name: Observer reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the device, sensor, process or person that made the observation.

data_elements.name: Observer kind
data_elements.description: Whether the observer is a device, a human, or a computational process.

data_elements.name: Responsible organisation reference
data_elements.description: Organisation accountable for the reported value.

findings.name: Uncertainty components and evaluation type
findings.description: The GUM distinguishes Type A evaluation by statistical analysis of repeated observations from Type B evaluation by other means; each component's distribution and degrees of freedom shape the combined result.

data_elements.name: Uncertainty component
data_elements.description: One contributing component with its standard uncertainty and evaluation basis.

data_elements.name: Evaluation type
data_elements.description: Type A or Type B designation for a component.

data_elements.name: Assumed distribution
data_elements.description: Probability distribution assumed for a component.

data_elements.name: Degrees of freedom
data_elements.description: Degrees of freedom or effective degrees of freedom supporting the coverage factor.

findings.name: Reported uncertainty and coverage statement
findings.description: GUM clause 7 requires a reported result to identify whether the stated uncertainty is standard, combined or expanded, and for expanded uncertainty to state the coverage factor and the level of confidence.

data_elements.name: Uncertainty value
data_elements.description: The reported uncertainty as a quantity, absolute or relative.

data_elements.name: Uncertainty type
data_elements.description: Standard, combined standard or expanded uncertainty.

data_elements.name: Coverage factor
data_elements.description: Multiplier k applied to the combined standard uncertainty.

data_elements.name: Coverage probability
data_elements.description: Level of confidence associated with the expanded uncertainty interval.

findings.name: Detection limits and censored values
findings.description: Regulators require a determined, method-specific detection limit, and FHIR carries a comparator on a Quantity; together they let a below-limit result be recorded without being mistaken for zero.

data_elements.name: Detection limit
data_elements.description: Method-specific limit below which the analyte or signal is not reliably distinguished from background.

data_elements.name: Quantitation limit
data_elements.description: Limit above the detection limit at which a value may be reported as a number.

data_elements.name: Censoring operator
data_elements.description: Comparator carried with a bounded value, such as less-than or greater-than-or-equal.

data_elements.name: Censoring basis
data_elements.description: Why the value is censored and against which limit.

findings.name: Interpretation flags and reference context
findings.description: FHIR carries interpretation codes and reference ranges, and SensorThings carries resultQuality; these are context that supports a reader, not a conformity decision, which JCGM 106 treats as a separate discipline.

data_elements.name: Interpretation code
data_elements.description: Coded qualitative reading of the value such as high, low or normal.

data_elements.name: Reference range reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the interval or threshold set applied when interpreting the value.

data_elements.name: Result quality assessment
data_elements.description: Coded quality outcomes attached to the result, as distinct from uncertainty.

findings.name: Phenomenon time, result time and ingestion time
findings.description: SOSA defines phenomenon time as the time the result applies to the feature of interest and result time as the instant the activity completed; the time the record entered a store is a third, distinct anchor.

data_elements.name: Phenomenon time
data_elements.description: Instant the result applies to the feature of interest.

data_elements.name: Phenomenon period
data_elements.description: Interval the result applies to when the phenomenon is not instantaneous.

data_elements.name: Result time
data_elements.description: Instant the observation activity completed and the result became available.

data_elements.name: Ingestion time
data_elements.description: Instant the result record entered the adopting store.

findings.name: Validity window and aggregation period
findings.description: SensorThings carries validTime for the period a result is valid; a value may also be a statistic over an interval rather than an instantaneous reading, which changes its meaning entirely.

data_elements.name: Valid time window
data_elements.description: Start and end of the period for which the result is asserted valid.

data_elements.name: Aggregation function
data_elements.description: Statistic applied when the value summarises an interval.

data_elements.name: Aggregation period
data_elements.description: Duration over which the statistic was computed.

findings.name: Status, amendment and supersession
findings.description: FHIR defines a status lifecycle from registered and preliminary through final, amended and entered-in-error; a corrected result must link to what it replaces rather than overwrite it.

data_elements.name: Result status
data_elements.description: Lifecycle status of the result record.

data_elements.name: Supersedes reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the result version this record replaces.

data_elements.name: Status changed at
data_elements.description: Time of the most recent status transition.

data_elements.name: Amendment reason
data_elements.description: Stated reason for an amendment, correction or withdrawal.

findings.name: Coded absence of a value
findings.description: FHIR requires a coded dataAbsentReason when no value is present; absence must be distinguishable from zero, from an empty string and from a censored value.

data_elements.name: Data absent reason
data_elements.description: Coded explanation for the absence of a value.

data_elements.name: Absence blocking indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the absence prevents downstream use of the record.

findings.name: Derivation, correction and assertion
findings.description: A reported value is often a corrected or derived quantity; PROV-O separates the entity's derivation from the agent to which it is attributed, and VIM notes that a result may be an indication, an uncorrected result or a corrected result.

data_elements.name: Derived-from reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a prior value or raw indication this result was derived from.

data_elements.name: Correction record
data_elements.description: Correction applied to the indication, with its basis.

data_elements.name: Asserting agent reference
data_elements.description: Agent responsible for asserting the result record.

findings.name: Evidence backing the reported value
findings.description: Raw captures and uncertainty budgets exist as separable objects with their own media, identity and integrity requirements, and are bound to the result by reference and digest.

data_elements.name: Evidence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an artifact substantiating the result.

data_elements.name: Evidence digest
data_elements.description: Cryptographic digest of the referenced evidence with its algorithm named.

data_elements.name: Evidence media type
data_elements.description: Media type or form of the referenced evidence item.

findings.name: Standard alignment and code-system versioning
findings.description: Alignment to OMS, SOSA/SSN, SensorThings, FHIR, UCUM and QUDT is a mapping rather than a conformance claim; each mapped code system evolves independently and must be version-pinned per record.

data_elements.name: Alignment target
data_elements.description: External standard or vocabulary this field group is mapped to.

data_elements.name: Conformance claim status
data_elements.description: Whether conformance is claimed with evidence, mapped only, or explicitly not claimed.

data_elements.name: Code system version pin
data_elements.description: Version of each referenced code system fixed at record creation.

findings.name: Projection and round-trip fidelity
findings.description: The same result must project into OMS, SOSA/SSN, SensorThings and FHIR shapes; each projection loses something (for example SensorThings binds the unit at Datastream level, not per observation) and that loss must be declared rather than discovered.

data_elements.name: Projection target
data_elements.description: Named exchange encoding the result is projected into.

data_elements.name: Lossy field list
data_elements.description: Fields lost or approximated for a given projection target.

data_elements.name: Payload digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical form used to detect payload change.

findings.name: Sensitivity classification and redaction signalling
findings.description: A value may be more sensitive than its host record; the mixin classifies and signals redaction so that a consumer never mistakes a redacted result for a complete one, while all evaluation stays with the access model.

data_elements.name: Sensitivity classification
data_elements.description: Classification code governing disclosure of the value.

data_elements.name: Redaction applied indicator
data_elements.description: Whether any part of the field group has been redacted in this representation.

data_elements.name: Disclosure basis reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the policy, contract or legal basis restricting disclosure.

functions.name: Bind result fields to a host record type
functions.description: Attaches the field group to a host record type under a named, versioned binding profile that fixes value kinds, unit code systems, mandatory fields and namespace prefix.

functions.name: Validate unit against quantity kind
functions.description: Checks that the recorded unit code resolves in the pinned code system and that its dimension is commensurable with the declared quantity kind of the observed property.

functions.name: Record a canonical-unit expression
functions.description: Stores a derived canonical-unit expression alongside the unchanged as-reported value, using a conversion factor resolved from the referenced unit registry.

functions.name: Assemble and check an uncertainty statement
functions.description: Assembles the GUM-shaped uncertainty statement from declared components and checks it for completeness and internal consistency; numerical propagation through the measurement model is performed by the producing measurement system, not by this model.

functions.name: Assert reporting completeness
functions.description: Evaluates a result record against the mandatory descriptor set of its binding profile before the record may be promoted to a final, publishable state.

functions.name: Record an absent or censored value
functions.description: Records a coded absence reason, or a bounded value with its comparator and the applicable limit, without substituting a numeric sentinel.

functions.name: Supersede a result with a corrected version
functions.description: Creates a new result version linked to the record it replaces, with an amendment reason and status transition, leaving the prior version retrievable.

functions.name: Project a result into an exchange profile
functions.description: Emits the field group into a registered target encoding and reports every field lost or approximated by that mapping.

functions.name: Assess comparability of results
functions.description: Advisory check of whether two or more result records may be directly compared, based on measurand specification, unit commensurability, method reference and time anchors.

functions.name: Verify evidence binding and integrity
functions.description: Re-computes and compares the digest of each referenced evidence item and records the verification outcome against the result.

composition.target: WM-MAT-008 (registered parent model)
composition.purpose: This field group is registered as a child of WM-MAT-008 and supplies the result payload fields its property records carry; the parent owns the record type, its subject and its lifecycle.

composition.target: Host record models adopting the field group (any model carrying observed or measured properties)
composition.purpose: Hosts embed the group under a versioned binding profile; the host owns the record, its identity and its access class, while this model owns only the field semantics and their validation rules.

composition.target: Unit and quantity-kind vocabulary registry (UCUM, QUDT, UN/CEFACT Rec 20)
composition.purpose: Supplies unit codes, quantity kinds, dimension vectors and conversion factors. This model pins a code-system version and cites codes; it never mints, deprecates or maintains them and holds no local copy of the conversion tables.

composition.target: Observed-property and observable vocabulary registry
composition.purpose: Supplies the observed-property codes and their expected quantity kinds and permissible value sets; this model carries the code, the code system and the version pin only.

composition.target: Procedure and method catalogue model
composition.purpose: Supplies method identity, versions, defaults and validation studies. This model carries the reference, the version and subject-specific parameter overrides, and never reproduces method authoring or approval lifecycle.

composition.target: Sensor, device and calibration record model
composition.purpose: Supplies observer identity and calibration records. This model carries the reference and a validity-at-observation check; device lifecycle, calibration execution and certificate issuance remain with the target.

composition.target: Feature-of-interest, sample and specimen model
composition.purpose: Anchors what the value is about. This model carries the reference and a proximate-versus-ultimate subject flag, not sample identity, hierarchy or custody.

composition.target: Agent, party and organisation identity model
composition.purpose: Supplies observer, asserter and accountable-organisation identities; this model carries references and role codes only.

composition.target: Access policy, audit and retention model of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Receives the sensitivity classification, retention class and policy reference recorded here and owns policy evaluation, enforcement, audit-trail storage and disposition execution. This model supplies audit event content but never evaluates, enforces or stores the trail.

composition.target: Time-series and statistical dataset model
composition.purpose: Holds series and waveform payloads that a result may point to; this model carries the series reference plus the sampling and aggregation descriptors needed to interpret it.

composition.target: Conformity assessment and decision-rule model
composition.purpose: Consumes values, uncertainties and limits to make acceptance decisions under a decision rule; this model supplies inputs and interpretation context and never records the conformity decision or its guard bands.

composition.target: JCGM measurement uncertainty framework (GUM JCGM 100:2008 and VIM JCGM 200:2012)
composition.purpose: Field names and semantics for measurand, measured quantity value, standard, combined and expanded uncertainty, evaluation type, coverage factor and coverage probability follow GUM and VIM terminology; this is a documented mapping, not a conformance claim.

composition.target: OGC/ISO Observations, Measurements and Samples and W3C SOSA/SSN
composition.purpose: Observed property, procedure, feature of interest, phenomenon time and result time map to OMS and SOSA constructs so that a hosted result can be exposed as an observation result without re-modelling the observation act.

composition.target: HL7 FHIR Observation and Quantity datatype
composition.purpose: Value polymorphism, comparator, absence coding, interpretation, component structure and status lifecycle map to FHIR equivalents for cross-domain exchange; FHIR resource-level security and audit semantics are explicitly not adopted.

composition.target: W3C PROV-O provenance vocabulary
composition.purpose: Derivation, attribution and generation-time fields map to wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith and generatedAtTime; the provenance graph store and its query semantics remain external.

providerPolicy.scope: Queued subject-model research from WM-XCT-013 onward

waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two distinct axes must not be collapsed. The frozen registry classifies the RECORD plane (record_plane world-model, registry_id vr.wm-xct-025, origin claude-plus-gap-audit, status candidate, review_state boundary-review-required); a record-plane value never determines the subject-model kind. On the SUBJECT axis the registry's 'mixin' is coincidentally also a valid schema enum value, and it is independently the most defensible kind: the subject declares no standalone record, defines an attachment point, cardinality, mandatory subset and namespace per host, is hosted by registered parent WM-MAT-008 plus any adopting host, is governed by a versioned binding profile artifact, and carries a namespace guidance (<dimension>.observable-result.*) whose only purpose is collision-free embedding. 'entity' was the serious rival, because the pack carries a status lifecycle, supersession, tombstone, full CRUD and retention language that reads like an owned record; it is rejected because those verbs operate on the host record the group is embedded in, and the pack's own duplication check states WM-MAT-008 owns the record type, subject and lifecycle while this model adds only result fields and their validation. 'pattern' is rejected as too weak: the group fixes mandatory fields, canonicalisation, digest scope and blocking validation gates, not merely a recurring shape. 'aggregate' is rejected because a mixin has no aggregate root of its own. Acceptance is conditional: the synthesizer must restate every record-lifecycle verb (create, supersede, withdraw, tombstone, retain, delete) as a host-scoped obligation the group qualifies, and must state explicitly whether a field-group instance is separately identified and versioned or shares the host identifier.

decisions.concept: Entry kind 'mixin' on the subject axis
decisions.rationale: Scope statement, attachment-contract finding, binding-profile artifact and namespace guidance are all coherent only under a mixin reading, and the frozen registry value happens to be a valid schema kind. Condition: record-plane and subject-plane classification must be stated separately in the published spec so the coincidence is not read as derivation.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root of the subject model
decisions.disposition: accepted as the host record, not the field group
decisions.rationale: A mixin has no root of its own. The pack states the host owns record identity, access class and retention, but crud.delete, patch_rules and supersede-result speak of 'result records' with their own identifier and supersession chain. The synthesizer must rewrite those as host-scoped obligations rather than an independent record lifecycle.

decisions.concept: Identity of a field-group instance
decisions.rationale: The checklist says the group inherits host identity, yet tombstones retain 'the identifier, the supersession chain' and patch rules version the value independently. No question in the 100 asks whether the group instance is separately identified or who mints that identifier. This must be answered before the identity dimension can stay marked covered.

decisions.concept: Claim of 'fourteen composition links' in the relationships checklist
decisions.rationale: The frozen relationship contract is an empty array and the registry record has empty contains_ids, aligned_model_ids and relations_ref. Eight boundary notes exist, not fourteen typed links. The count must be deleted or the links materialised in the contract; an uncorroborated count is exactly the kind of claim a waived second provider would have caught.

decisions.concept: Parent relation to WM-MAT-008
decisions.rationale: parent_ids names WM-MAT-008 and the scope statement calls it the registered parent host, but the relationship contract carries nothing. The hosted-by relation is the model's single load-bearing composition claim and must be written into the contract before status advances past candidate.

decisions.concept: access.scopes = bundle / layer / finding / artifact
decisions.rationale: Those four are research-record planes describing this world-model document, not planes of the modelled result data. Subject-plane scopes should be host record, field-group instance, individual field or value, and evidence artifact. As written the access section grants scopes over the specification rather than over results.

decisions.concept: Indivisible read set versus restricted uncertainty
decisions.rationale: crud.read requires value, unit, measurand, time anchors and uncertainty to return as one indivisible set, while access.exceptions permits uncertainty budgets and method parameters to be restricted for proprietary methods. The indivisible set must be redefined to include an explicit restricted-uncertainty marker so the two rules stop contradicting each other.

decisions.concept: Privacy erasure in place versus the never-in-place patch rule
decisions.disposition: accepted with a required named exception
decisions.rationale: patch_rules state a change to value is never an in-place patch, yet crud.delete redacts the value, evidence references and digests in place under an erasure obligation. The exception must be named in patch_rules, and the fate of the pre-erasure canonical digest decided explicitly: retaining it preserves integrity verification but may itself be the identifying residue erasure targets.

decisions.concept: Serial artifact naming embedding an observed-property code and sequence
decisions.rationale: identity_priority forbids sequence position and governed codes from acting as identifiers, and forbids identifiers encoding pinned code-system versions, yet serial_naming_rule builds names from host id, observed-property code and sequence. artifact_rules must state normatively that this serial name is a display and ordering label and never an identifier, and must pin or slot-key the code component.

decisions.concept: Artifact discipline: 3 artifacts on 2 findings, 23 inline-only rationales
decisions.rationale: Recounted against the delivered structure: supporting-evidence-records carries two artifacts, alignment-and-code-system-versioning carries one, both with null inline_only_rationale, and the remaining twenty-three findings carry empty arrays with substantive rationales. No finding populates both. The self-reported adversarial artifact audit is accurate.

decisions.concept: SRC-012 JCGM publication index cited as a tier-1 primary source
decisions.rationale: A publication index page accessed on 3 September 2026 is a locator, not normative text, yet it backs clause-level claims about uncertainty reporting and about conformity assessment being a separate discipline. Replace with clause-anchored citations to JCGM 106:2012 and the relevant GUM documents, or downgrade its primary_source flag.

decisions.concept: SRC-008 QUDT (authority tier 3) anchoring a blocking commensurability check
decisions.rationale: validate-unit-quantity-consistency rejects records at creation on the strength of a dimension vector, and the highest-authority backing for that rejection should be the SI Brochure and VIM. QUDT should be cited as the computable encoding of that requirement, with the dimension-vector field marked vocabulary-dependent and version-pinned.

decisions.concept: bind-result-fields citing the FHIR Observation resource page for a profiling capability
decisions.rationale: Attaching a versioned field group to a host type is a profiling and conformance mechanism, not something the Observation resource page establishes. Either cite FHIR conformance and profiling material, or declare the binding mechanism Vercy-internal and make no external support claim for it.

decisions.concept: record-canonical-expression without a refusal precondition
decisions.rationale: The model asks q-canon-refuse and q-qk-offset-units, and policies forbid coercion, but the function itself carries no precondition. Offset and non-ratio scales such as degrees Celsius, and ordinal or nominal properties, are precisely where a silent conversion corrupts arithmetic. The refusal condition must be stated on the function, not only asked in a question.

decisions.concept: Missing code-system migration and redaction-emission functions
decisions.rationale: crud.update and compatibility_rules both mandate an explicit logged migration for a code-system re-pin, and crud.read mandates redaction indicators and coarsened substitutes, but neither obligation has a corresponding function among the ten. Single-provider mode forbids adding functions here, so this is logged for the next revision rather than patched now.

decisions.concept: Retention questions phrased as durations
decisions.rationale: q-state-history and q-evid-retention ask how long records must be kept, while the model delegates retention periods, legal holds and disposition entirely to the adopting Dimension and records only a retention class. Restate both as retention-class selection questions so the model does not appear to set periods it disclaims owning.

decisions.concept: ISO/IEC 17025 clause 7.8 recorded as unverifiable rather than asserted
decisions.rationale: Declining to claim test-report conformance because the primary text is paywalled is correct falsifiability discipline and is the strongest single signal that the pack was not padded. Preserve the disclaimer unchanged in every published artifact rather than softening it to an alignment claim.

publicationHolds: Live source and version verification hold: none of the thirteen source URLs, version pins or status claims were checked by this audit. Before publication, verify live and date-stamp at minimum UCUM 2.2 dated 17 June 2024, FHIR R5 Observation and the claim that Observation has been normative since R4, OGC 20-082r4 / OMS 3.0 and its ISO 19156:2023 alignment, SSN/SOSA as still the current Recommendation, QUDT 2.1 (whose stated date is a site-generation date, not a release date), SensorThings 1.1, and the JCGM documents cited through the publication index.

Single-provider hold: publish only as a reviewable draft carrying a visible notice that independent second-provider review was waived by the repository owner on 2026-08-29T09:06:27Z after repeated Grok structured-output failures, that this Claude-only result received a no-tools adversarial audit rather than corroboration, and that entry_kind, boundary and artifact decisions rest on a single provider's structure with no cross-check.

Relationship hold: the checklist claim of fourteen composition links is unsupported by the frozen relationship contract, which is empty, and the WM-MAT-008 hosting relation exists only in the registry record. Either materialise the links and the parent relation in the contract or remove the count before publication.

Aggregate-root hold: record-lifecycle language (create, supersede, withdraw, tombstone, retain, hard-delete) must be rewritten as host-scoped obligations, and the question of whether a field-group instance carries its own identifier and version must be answered, before the identity and lifecycle checklist dimensions may remain marked covered.

Registry-state hold: the frozen record is status candidate with review_state boundary-review-required. Record this adversarial audit as the boundary review, keep status at candidate, and do not advance review_state until the source-verification, relationship and aggregate-root holds are cleared.
Independent second-provider review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this Claude-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Close the declared limits-and-censoring gap: verify cross-domain detection and quantitation limit determination against primary text from IUPAC, ISO 11843 and clinical limit-of-blank / detection / quantitation conventions, so the semantics do not rest solely on a United States Clean Water Act procedure.

Close the declared measurement-scale-type gap: find a verifiable cross-domain primary source for scale type (nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio) and for permitted arithmetic on ordinal codes; the nominal-property counterexample in the pack's own adversarial check depends on this provisional field.

Obtain licensed access to ISO/IEC 17025 clause 7.8 to confirm that the deliberate non-claim about test-report conformance remains correct and that no mandatory reporting element is silently missing from the mandatory descriptor set.

Decide whether correlation and covariance between uncertainty components or output quantities belong in this field group at all, or wholly in the producing measurement system, and record the decision rather than leaving multivariate results as components with no covariance structure.

Re-verify whether SSN/SOSA has moved beyond the 2017 Recommendation in a way that changes resultTime typing, since the model's divergence on offset-free timestamps is stated as a conflict against that specific version.

Resolve the two missing functions in a later revision: an explicit code-system re-pin migration function required by crud.update and compatibility_rules, and a redaction-emission function required by crud.read, neither of which could be added under single-provider rules.

Determine whether a normative rounding algorithm can be sourced at all, or whether the current 'named but not mandated' position is permanent; the pack leaves rounding unresolved for lack of a verified cross-domain source while still requiring trailing-zero precision to survive round trips.

limits: Both bases are non-canonical reviewable drafts; complete specs were parsed and pinned.
Metric Definition from EM-DAT-05 and benefit/value mastership are not allocated in these two reservations.
